answer: Honeypot canary tasks resist sybil grading rings: the system seeds grading queues with planted items whose correct verdict is known only to the protocol, indistinguishable from real work like a comet hidden among stars. A ring told to rubber-stamp its own answers will approve the planted bad item too, and any grader passing a honeypot is flagged and slashed. Honest graders judge the canary on merits and reject it; a sybil cluster on a sonnet-scripted approve-everything strategy cannot tell the karst-grey decoy from genuine work, so ring behavior leaks a detectable false-approval rate.
